speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a dermatological concern; please describe the specific lesions you are worried about, including their size, color, and any changes you have noticed recently. To help me evaluate the potential for malignancy, do you have any personal or family history of skin cancer?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient describes a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the penile shaft and a similar lesion on the left middle finger. Given the history of heavy smoking and lack of response to previous treatments, we must urgently rule out malignancy. REQUEST TEST: Tumor markers and biopsy of the penile lesion.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy findings indicate cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium. STD Panel (Syphilis, HIV, HBV, HCV) is negative.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

The biopsy confirms malignant features with nuclear hyperchromasia and increased mitosis, and the negative STD panel rules out infectious causes like syphilis. Given your history of heavy smoking and the non-healing nature of the lesions, this is consistent with Squamous Cell Carcinoma affecting both the penile shaft and the digit.
